chunks: From him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-'Is ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
"The traveler remains in a state of shortening (prayer) until he enters his house."

key_terms.الْمُسَافِرُ: The traveler (one eligible for shortening prayers)
key_terms.مُقَصِّراً: Shortening (referring to the reduction of rak'ahs in prayer)
key_terms.يَدْخُلَ بَيْتَهُ: Enters his house (the condition for ending the travel status)

ai.seo_question: When does a traveler's obligation to shorten prayers end according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the precise boundary for the traveler's status (*hukm al-musafir*), establishing that the concession of *qasr* (shortening four-rak'ah prayers to two) persists until the traveler physically enters their domicile. In Shia jurisprudence, this definition prevents premature resumption of full prayers and underscores the importance of the 'home' as the threshold for returning to the standard state of worship.
